constraints: Opening a barrier gate is restricted to operators holding the gate:operate permission.
The unknown-floor condition and the already-open-gate condition must be signalled as two distinguishable exceptions, not one shared error.
Opening the entry gate requires a vehicle plate number to be supplied.
Queries (floor occupancy, gate status) carry no stated permission requirement, unlike gate opening.

entities.description: The remaining-capacity report for one floor of the parking facility.

fields.name: level
fields.shape: floor identifier as the requirement names it — a floor the caller can ask about, and which may be unknown to the system

fields.name: remaining_spaces
fields.shape: count of parking spaces still free on that floor

entities.name: FloorOccupancy

entities.description: A barrier gate at the facility, whose status can be read and which can be opened.

fields.name: gate_id
fields.shape: identifier of the gate as the requirement leaves it unspecified

fields.name: state
fields.shape: gate status — the requirement distinguishes at least open from not-open

entities.name: BarrierGate

entities.description: The vehicle presented at the entry gate, identified by its plate number.

fields.name: plate_number
fields.shape: vehicle registration plate number as printed on the vehicle

entities.name: VehicleEntry

open_questions: The requirement does not say how floors are identified — a signed level number that can be negative for basements (B1, B2), or a string label. This decides whether 'unknown floor' means out-of-range or unrecognised label.
It does not say whether floor occupancy is queried one floor at a time or returned for all floors at once; the summary phrase '층별' could mean either.

It does not say how gates are addressed for the status query, nor how many gates exist — the open operation names only the entry gate, but the status query says 'barrier gate status' without restricting it to entry.
It does not say whether there is a corresponding exit gate or a close operation. No close/exit operation was invented here.
It does not state what the open operation returns — nothing, a ticket/entry record, or an assigned floor or space.
It does not say whether re-opening an already-open gate is an error only for the entry gate or for any gate, nor whether an already-closed gate is likewise a distinct condition.
It does not state the plate-number format, character set (Korean plates contain Hangul), or maximum length.
It does not say whether the caller's identity/permission arrives as an operation parameter, a service context, or an out-of-band security layer — this materially changes the operation signature.
It does not state whether the total capacity per floor, or only the remaining count, is exposed.

It does not say whether opening the gate should be retry-safe; the effect is left 'unspecified' because a second call is explicitly an error condition rather than a silent no-op, which is not the same as idempotent.

errors: unknown floor — reported as its own distinct exception
operations.name: get_floor_occupancy

outputs.name: occupancy
outputs.shape: remaining parking space count for that floor

inputs.name: target_gate
inputs.shape: which gate to read, as the requirement does not say how gates are addressed

outputs.name: status
outputs.shape: current status of that barrier gate

errors: gate already open — reported as its own distinct exception, separate from the unknown-floor exception

inputs.name: plate_number
inputs.shape: vehicle plate number the entry is granted for

operations.name: open_entry_gate

requirement: 주차장 관제. 층별 잔여 주차면 수와 차단기 상태를 조회하고, 차량번호를 지정해 입차 차단기를 연다. 차단기 개방은 gate:operate 권한을 가진 운영자만 할 수 있다. 알 수 없는 층과 이미 열려 있는 차단기는 각각 구분해 예외로 알린다.
summary: A parking-facility control interface for querying per-floor remaining space counts and barrier-gate status, and for opening the entry gate for a specified vehicle plate number.
